items.reason: Lift flows from preset decoding through build options to row ordering and marking.
Only the shipped active preset declares Lift true.
The pin alias sets Lift without warnings or deprecation findings.
When both keys appear, lift determines the grant.
Omitting both spellings leaves Lift false.
A non-bool pin produces no finding when lift is also present because decoding stops after lift.
The assertNothingPinned helper remains in dashboardshell/work_lift_test.go and names derived ordering as pinning.
The diff preserves the manual and unrelated pin terminology and behavior.
The field metadata and shipped grant use lift; pin is retained only for decoding compatibility.
Repository attribution covers sibling worktrees, with a real-worktree regression test.
Checkout attribution returns before repository attribution and retains its existing ranking.
Task-set tags retain first-pass precedence over repository work.
Repository candidates include both bound and unbound Task sets.
Repository candidates are filtered by canonical git common directory.
Both kinds discard duplicate IDs across repositories, and cursor keys still collide on identical project names and IDs.
Missing or unknown repository identities yield no attribution, lifted rows, or status message.
The repository pass concatenates every answering kind, explicitly tested with Task sets and Maps.
Launch resolves repository identity once; a counting git seam asserts no additional attribution calls over five rebuilds.
Status builds use empty pane facts, with a test rejecting repository-attribution git calls.
Attribution cannot reintroduce rows removed by the preset, and narrowing remains unchanged.
Repository locality selects active, non-broken Maps; shipped preset filtering prevents hidden Maps from lifting.
Combined attribution lifts Task sets before Maps, covered by a concrete two-kind snapshot test.
Map session stamps return before the weaker repository pass, with regression coverage.
Routines implement neither locality seam, and an explicit comment explains the deliberate asymmetry.

scores.rationale: Clear architecture and substantial regression coverage, but repository collisions, incomplete alias validation, and a missed rename leave acceptance gaps.
